today.h: Chips -5.3% Into the Verdict: Nasdaq -2.49%, a Correction
today.d: The AI trade's defining week opened with a 5.28% drop in the SOX and a 4.12% fall in Nvidia, leaving the Nasdaq 2.49% lower at 24,509.76 - 11.19% below its 10/6 record close and in a correction - while the S&P 500 lost 145.08 points to 7,416.59 and the Dow 739.38 points. The VIX rose 18.70% to 22.91, and the bond market barely moved: the 10Y fell 3bp to 5.12% as Brent settled 3.55% lower at $92.44.
today.c1: The market's biggest week of the quarter started with the AI complex selling itself. Nvidia fell 4.12% to $156.14 - 34.7% below its 10/6 record - as the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation entered a second week, the Commerce Department moved to restrict remote access to advanced US chips and servers, and traders cut exposure before Tuesday's earnings. The damage was hardware-wide: Micron 7.62%, Marvell 7.27%, Intel 7.02%, AMD 5.58% and Broadcom 3.92%, with Lumentum 8.48% and SanDisk 8.58% the S&P's worst. The Nasdaq Composite closed 11.19% below its 10/6 record, a correction by the standard definition, while the S&P fell 1.92%, its third straight loss and the biggest three-session drop since June. Nine of 11 sectors fell; only consumer staples (+0.27%) and utilities (+0.18%) closed green. The rate market offered no rescue: the 10Y fell just 3bp, gold settled at its lowest since October 2025 and the dollar held near a 19-month high, because the driver is a December hike now about 92% priced, not growth fear.
today.c4:
• The concentration: Nvidia -4.12% and a 5.28% SOX drop explain the 2.49% Nasdaq loss; the Dow fell 1.41%.
  • The tell: only staples and utilities closed higher, and Tyson's 8.72% led the index.
  • The rates: a 3bp fall at the 10Y is not a haven bid, and gold's lowest settle since October 2025 says the same.
  • The calendar: Nvidia earnings 11/17 after the close, retail sales 11/17, FOMC minutes 11/18, Anthropic prices 11/18 and trades 11/19, FOMC 12/8-9.
